summary: orderly-plugin-liquidity-heatmap postinstall abuses CI GITHUB_TOKEN to commit to installer repo and harvests runner metadata
details: The package's main export (dist/index.js) is a one-line stub, while scripts/setup.js runs as a postinstall and is the package's actual payload. When executed inside a GitHub Actions runner (gated on CI + GITHUB_WORKSPACE), it: (1) reads the runner's GITHUB_TOKEN and issues an authenticated PUT to https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/contents/heatmap-setup-report.json, writing a commit into the installer's default branch under the installer's own identity; (2) collects hostname, OS, user, cwd, GITHUB_REPOSITORY/WORKFLOW, enumerates process.env keys starting with GITHUB_/ACTIONS_/RUNNER_, records token lengths and OIDC request URL/token presence, and publishes this snapshot to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and into the committed report file; (3) probes the GitHub Actions OIDC endpoint by curling ${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=api.github.com with the Bearer ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN header. The README describes the postinstall as 'pre-caching asset paths', which does not match the observed behavior. Demonstrated repository-write access via the installer's CI credential, coupled with runner-secret-adjacent reconnaissance and OIDC minting probes, constitutes an attack on CI pipelines that install this package.
